name: Battle of Midway

phases.title: The fleets take their places
phases.text: Nimitz sent Fletcher's force to the Midway area before the Japanese arrived, and the two American task forces waited northeast of the atoll. Nagumo's carriers approached from the west, with Yamamoto's ships several hundred miles behind them.

phases.title: The Japanese strike Midway
phases.text: Nagumo launched his first attack on Midway at 04:30, with 36 dive bombers and 36 torpedo bombers escorted by 36 Zeros. Marine fighters from the island intercepted it, and the base was bombed from 06:34, though most of its defences stayed intact.

phases.title: Midway's bombers attack the carriers
phases.text: American bombers that had taken off from Midway before the Japanese attack made several attacks on the Japanese carrier force. The Japanese repelled them, losing only three Zero fighters.

phases.title: The American carriers launch their strikes
phases.text: Enterprise and Hornet began launching a few minutes after 07:00, steaming away from the Japanese to launch into the wind, and Yorktown followed at 08:00. Spruance sent his aircraft off piecemeal rather than wait for them to assemble.

phases.title: American torpedo squadrons are shot down
phases.text: Torpedo Squadron 8 sighted the Japanese carriers and attacked at 09:20 without fighter escort, and all 15 of its aircraft were shot down. Torpedo Squadron 6 lost 9 of its 14. All their torpedoes missed or failed to explode.

phases.title: Yorktown's torpedo squadron draws the fighters off
phases.text: Yorktown's torpedo squadron VT-3 attacked from the southeast, and 10 of its 12 aircraft were shot down without a hit. Its appearance drew most of the Japanese fighter patrol to that side of the fleet, leaving it out of position.

phases.title: Dive bombers set Kaga ablaze
phases.text: Both of Enterprise's dive-bomber squadrons dived at Kaga by mistake, and she took three to five direct hits. One bomb killed her captain and most of her senior officers, and she was ablaze from stem to stern within six minutes.

phases.title: Akagi and Sōryū are hit
phases.text: Lieutenant Best and his two wingmen dived on Akagi, which took a single bomb that exploded among the armed and fuelled aircraft. At the same time Yorktown's VB-3 hit Sōryū at least three times. All three carriers were eventually abandoned and scuttled.

phases.title: Hiryū's first wave hits Yorktown
phases.text: Hiryū, the one carrier still operating, sent 18 dive bombers and 6 Zeros after the retreating American aircraft. They found Yorktown and hit her with three bombs, and Fletcher moved his command staff to the heavy cruiser Astoria.

phases.title: Hiryū's second wave cripples Yorktown
phases.text: About an hour later ten torpedo bombers and six Zeros arrived. Yorktown's repairs had been so effective that the Japanese pilots took her for a different carrier. Two torpedoes crippled her, and she lost all power and listed 23 degrees to port.

phases.title: Enterprise's bombers cripple Hiryū
phases.text: A Yorktown scout found Hiryū, and Enterprise launched 24 dive bombers. Four bombs, possibly five, hit her and left her ablaze. She stayed afloat for several hours and sank after being spotted the next morning.

phases.title: Spruance withdraws to the east
phases.text: Spruance, fearing a possible night encounter with Japanese surface forces, changed course and withdrew to the east. He turned back west towards the Japanese at midnight.

phases.title: Yamamoto sends his ships east
phases.text: Yamamoto at first decided to continue the engagement and sent his remaining surface forces searching eastward for the American carriers. At the same time he detached a cruiser raiding force to bombard Midway.

phases.title: Yamamoto orders a general withdrawal
phases.text: The Japanese surface forces failed to make contact with the Americans, and Yamamoto ordered a general withdrawal to the west. His main body and the cruiser force turned back.

note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: each block is a fleet or a group of carriers, and the distances are schematic. Only the directions the account gives are kept: the Americans lay northeast of Midway and east of Nagumo's carriers, and Yamamoto's ships trailed Nagumo by several hundred miles. The attack groups of aircraft are drawn as arrows between the fleets that sent them.
